title: The impact of an online-based pelvic floor training on the health and health literacy of women and men - a prospective pre-post observational study
summary:
Women who have not done pelvic floor exercises during or after pregnancy often complain of poor posture, back problems, incontinence or organ prolapse. As a result, most women only come into contact with pelvic floor training once they have taken part in a postnatal course or their gynecologist has prescribed it. However, men can also experience incontinence disorders, poor posture and back pain. 
An observational study will investigate the effects of an online pelvic floor training program. The aim is to examine the program under conditions that are as realistic and practical as possible. The content of the intervention is offered in the form of a didactically prepared online course. Based on the objectives described, participants will learn tensing and strengthening exercises for the pelvic floor muscles as well as exercises to train their ability to relax. The practical units are supplemented with information and knowledge about the pelvic floor (including with the help of Behavior Change Techniques).

interventions.name: Users of the online-based pelvic floor training receive a total of four assessments: at the program's start, post-usage, and for two long-term evaluations after 6 and 12 months

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Users with special risks to the musculoskeletal system and motor control, particularly of the pelvic floor.
Users with risks in the area of the musculoskeletal system and in the area of motor control, especially in the area of the pelvic floor.
Exclusion criteria:
Symptoms of severe mental illness that interfere with the ability to participate; Severe chronic illness; Insufficient knowledge of the German language (i.e., unable to use the app and answer the questionnaire); Other reasons that prevent the correct use of the app and completion of the questions
